newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - AlliedSignal seeks growth boost.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - AlliedSignal seeks growth boost.

text.p: AlliedSignal Inc is looking to acquisitions to keep earnings growth near the high end of its 13 to 17 percent goal, Chief Executive Lawrence A. Bossidy said Thursday.

Stating "we'd like (profit growth) to be on the Northern end of the goal," he told Reuters the company is looking to niche acquistions to boost sales growth above eight percent increase expected from current operations.
Earlier the company reported first quarter profits were up 15 percent to a record $0.92 per share.
The profit growth, which matched the First Call consensus estimate, came on a three percent rise in sales from comparable operations to $3.33 billion.

Stating he is "convinced" AlliedSignal growth will achieve the company's goals, Bossidy said first quarter earnings were boosted by a business mix featuring "very high margin" operations. In particular he cited strong sales of aftermarket parts and repair and overhaul services by the company's Aerospace operations.
Although the company expects better sales growth during the rest of the year, the business mix will not provide the margins to maintain the first quarter earnings growth pace, he said.
In 1996, earnings increased 16 percent to $3.61 per share as sales increased eight percent to $1.02 billion.
Bossidy said AlliedSignal is looking to expected outsourcing by pharmaceutical companies and semiconductor makers to provide additional growth in sales.
He said the company's specialty chemical operations expect to get some of the business as pharmaceutical companies outsource agricultural products.
Other parts of AlliedSignal's Engineered Materials business are looking at taking on parts of the semiconductor manufacturing process for such companies as Intel Corp, Bossidy said.
Noting the company moved toward these markets with two niche acquisitions last year, he said it would like to make a couple more this year.
Pointing out these are "big margin businesses," he said the acquisitions "will be expensive."

Bossidy said the company will fund the acquistions from cash on hand while it continues to fund capital spending and research and development from cash flow at the rate of about $1 billion per year into the foreseeable future.
He said capital spending is expected to total $750 million this year, noting that is "a little over last year," while R&D continues at the $350 million pace.
He also said the company will buy back enough stock to keep the number of shares outstanding unchanged, noting this totaled seven million shares last year.
